source_locator: R2225: ch. VII, Aola Bay and the 8th Marines
current_activity: landing at Lunga Point with the reinforced 8th Marines
notes: Miller, ch. VII: Callaghan’s task force, delayed by nearby enemy forces, sailed into Sealark Channel on 4 November 1942 to debark the reinforced 8th Marines, including the 75-mm pack howitzers of the 1st Battalion, 10th Marines. The noon air attack forced the Lunga section to withdraw for the night and return the next morning to finish unloading. Miller also writes that troop strength increased with the addition of the 8th Marines on 4 November. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. The 10th Marines are not given a regiment-level claim (only the 1st Battalion is named).

source_locator: R2225: ch. VIII, Resumption of the Kokumbona Offensive
current_activity: attacking west of Point Cruz with the 2nd Marines and 1st Battalion, 164th Infantry
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: on 10 November, with the Koli force reduced, the newly arrived 8th Marines, the 2nd Marines (less 3rd Battalion), and 1st Battalion, 164th Infantry, moved west from Point Cruz in a frontal attack on a three-battalion front under Colonel Arthur, supported by battalions of the 11th Marines. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. Only 1st Battalion of the 164th was in this attack (2nd Battalion was still at Koli), so the 164th is not given a regiment-level claim for this day.

source_locator: R2225: ch. VIII, Resumption of the Kokumbona Offensive
current_activity: retiring across the Matanikau after the mid-November convoy warning
notes: Miller, ch. VIII: after a further advance on 11 November, Vandegrift halted the offensive because of Japanese troop convoys expected in mid-November. The 2nd and 8th Marines recrossed the Matanikau on 11 November, covered by 1st Battalion, 164th Infantry, which followed the next day, and the bridges were destroyed. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

notes: Miller, ch. XI: ten minutes after the 2nd Marines jumped off on 13 January 1943, the leading units of the 8th Marines on the right began the attack from the east slopes of Hills 80 and 81. Japanese fire in the ravines stopped the move. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XI, The Coastal Offensive; R2226: ch. IX, Coming of the 2d Division
current_activity: clearing the ravine to its front and taking its last assigned objective
notes: Miller, ch. XI, and Zimmerman, ch. IX, agree that on 17 January 1943 the 8th Marines completed their last assigned work on the coastal line. Miller says that by the end of 17 January the regiment had cleared the ravine to its front and advanced its line beside the 6th Marines (and was withdrawn on 18 January). Zimmerman says the 8th Marines had taken their last assigned objective by 0930 on 17 January and were likewise relieved and went into bivouac. Confidence 0.7 for the 17 January completion of the objective.
